issues.action: Replace CWAN with a live holding (or remove) in data/portfolios.json growth sleeve. Unresolved across every run since the closure was first identified (~06-28/06-30) -- escalating.

summary.headline: Iran conflict sharply escalates -- oil tankers struck off Saudi Arabia, Houthis claim Red Sea attacks, Iran's IRGC reports a mined-route tanker explosion near the Strait of Hormuz, and the US completed a 12th consecutive night of strikes; Brent topped $98.44 (+4.6%) and WTI ~$90, the highest since May/June -- remains the sole portfolio-level RED, still not de-escalating. GOOG's Q2 print landed with revenue/EPS beats but a large capex raise ($195-205B FY guide, up from $180-190B) that punished GOOG itself (negative free cash flow for the first time) -- the desk's AI-infra suppliers read it constructively instead (NVDA +2.3%, CRDO +2.0%, MRVL +1.5%, AMD +1.4%, TSM/LRCX roughly flat), resolving the standing hyperscaler-capex watch favorably. A reversal day for last week's high-flyers: COIN (-5.5%) and HRMY (-5.3%) both give back their prior-session pops with no new tier-1-confirmed catalyst identified; TEL (-4.2%) extends Tuesday's ~7% post-acquisition-announcement slide (Astrodyne TDI, $1.4B) despite a record Q3 beat -- a capital-allocation reaction, not a fundamental miss. FCX (+3.9%) reported Q2 results this morning and continues recovering from the earlier Grasberg-delay overhang. CWAN roster-integrity flag unresolved for a 29th day.

flags.headline: US-Iran conflict escalates further -- tankers struck, Brent tops $98
flags.detail: The Iran conflict intensified overnight rather than cooling: Houthi forces (Iran-backed) claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea after threatening a blockade; Iran's IRGC said one of three tankers attempting a 'mined route' south of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after an explosion, forcing the other two to turn back; and the US completed its 12th consecutive night of strikes aimed at degrading Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping. Brent crude gained 4.6% to $98.44/bbl (highest since late May) and WTI rose ~3.8% to $90.14 (highest since June 8), putting Brent on pace for a 35.3% monthly gain -- the third-largest in a decade. This is a portfolio-level macro overhang, not a single-name issue: it pressures broad risk sentiment while remaining a tailwind for the energy sleeve (CVX, OKE, CNX, VLO).

flags.headline: COIN -5.5%, giving back all of yesterday's CLARITY Act pop
flags.detail: Coinbase fell 5.53% to $166.07, fully reversing yesterday's +9.5% CLARITY Act-driven rally. Web search found no new negative tier-1 catalyst for today specifically -- the JPMorgan and Piper Sandler ($155 target, cut from $170) analyst actions cited in current coverage are from 2026-07-13/07-14 and were already known. Most likely explanation is profit-taking after the prior-session spike and/or broader crypto softness, but that is inference, not confirmed. Q2 earnings land 2026-07-30 (one week out) -- flagging the calendar approach.
flags.thesis_link: Loosely matches COIN key_risk: 'leveraged bet on crypto market sentiment' -- ordinary volatility around that risk, not a new event materializing.

flags.headline: HRMY -5.3%, giving back yesterday's post-preannouncement pop
flags.detail: Harmony Biosciences fell 5.31% to $34.87, reversing yesterday's +9.9% move. No new tier-1 news found for today; the record preliminary Q2 WAKIX revenue ($261M, +30% YoY) and CFO transition (Glenn Reicin departing, Stephen Mollichella interim) are both from 2026-07-16 and already priced through this week's swings. Full Q2 results are officially confirmed for 2026-08-04 (GlobeNewswire/BusinessWire), not this week as one aggregator implied -- flagging that discrepancy so the desk isn't caught off guard by a mis-dated earnings alert.

flags.headline: TEL -4.2% today, extending Tuesday's ~7% post-acquisition slide despite a beat
flags.detail: TE Connectivity fell another 4.18% to $200.36 today, on top of a nearly 7% decline on 2026-07-22 when it reported record Q3 FY2026 results (sales $5.16B, +14% YoY; adjusted EPS $2.94 vs. $2.87 est., a 2.4% beat) alongside a $1.4B agreement to acquire Astrodyne TDI. The two-day ~11% drawdown reads as a market reaction to the M&A capital-allocation decision, not a fundamental miss -- Barclays raised its price target to $300 (from $297, Overweight) after the print. Does not match a listed key_risk (those center on automotive cyclicality and AI-capex-linked valuation, not M&A), so no thesis escalation, but the magnitude across two sessions warrants desk awareness.

flags.headline: SYK -1.7%, Q2 print (07-30) remains the key test of cyber-incident recovery
flags.detail: Stryker eased 1.69% to $309.24 today, no fresh catalyst. Q2 earnings land 2026-07-30 (one week out) and will be the first hard read on whether the March 2026 'Handala' cybersecurity incident that disrupted production/logistics has been fully resolved, and whether the 8-9.5% organic growth guide is intact given the premium 22.4x forward multiple.
flags.thesis_link: Matches SYK key_risk: 'March 2026 cybersecurity incident by Handala hacker group disrupted production and logistics, raising concerns about IT infrastructure resilience and potential recurring cyber exposure.'

flags.headline: GPC calm today (+1.0%) but the Iran-driven input-cost risk it flagged is intensifying, not fading
flags.detail: Genuine Parts ticked up 0.99% to $120.36 today -- no fresh deterioration -- but management's H2 guidance caution (given on the 07-21 Q2 print) specifically cited Iran-conflict cost pressure, and that macro driver has gotten materially worse since (Brent +$6-7 in two sessions). Keeping this amber on the underlying driver rather than today's tape.
flags.thesis_link: Matches GPC key_risk: 'Razor-thin 3.4% net profit margin provides minimal buffer for tariff impacts, inflationary cost pressures ... or cyclical revenue softness' -- rising oil/input costs from the Iran conflict is exactly this risk.

flags.headline: MARA calm today (+1.4%); core BTC-leverage risk unchanged
flags.detail: MARA rose a modest 1.35% to $12.40, a quiet session after a volatile stretch. The underlying thesis risk (MARA's earnings are a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price, with $850M in convertible debt to service) is unchanged and not today's news -- carried forward as a standing watch item, not escalated.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means MARA's financial performance is essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price.'

flags.headline: GOOG's Q2 capex raise lands constructively for the desk's AI-infra suppliers
flags.detail: Alphabet beat on revenue ($119.8B vs. $116.93B est.) and Cloud grew 82%, but raised FY2026 capex guidance sharply to $195-205B (from $180-190B) and posted negative free cash flow for the first time as a public company -- GOOGL itself sank on the print. For the desk's holdings, though, the read was favorable: NVDA +2.33%, CRDO +1.97%, MRVL +1.52%, AMD +1.44% (all suppliers into the same AI-capex wave), with TSM -0.78% and LRCX -0.80% roughly flat. This resolves the standing hyperscaler-capex watch flagged over the past two weeks -- season's first big capex data point read as a positive for the picks-and-shovels names, not a negative.

flags.headline: FCX +3.9% on Q2 print, continuing to recover from the Grasberg overhang
flags.detail: Freeport-McMoRan reported Q2 results before today's open; shares rose 3.94% to $64.99. No new negative development -- the Grasberg Block Cave production delays that pressured the stock earlier in the year are known/priced, and today's move reads as continued recovery alongside copper strength (futures at a one-month high on China demand).

flags.headline: SUPV +5.6%, continuing its Argentina-reform-driven recovery
flags.detail: Grupo Supervielle rose 5.57% to $10.24, extending a positive stretch tied to Argentine credit-market reform momentum. No new negative catalyst.

flags.headline: AEM +4.1% as gold strength persists
flags.detail: Agnico Eagle rose 4.12% to $147.43, riding continued gold strength on Mideast-conflict safe-haven demand. No name-specific catalyst; consistent with the broader macro backdrop.

flags.headline: ADP resolved amber->green -- stabilized, no new catalyst
flags.detail: ADP eased a further 1.26% to $243.08, a much calmer session than the unconfirmed -3.6% drop flagged two sessions ago. No new negative development found; resolving this flag.

flags.headline: ATAT resolved amber->green -- bounced off its fresh 52-week low
flags.detail: ATAT rose 0.59% to $31.41, a small bounce after Monday's fresh 52-week low and the 07-14 Zacks downgrade to Hold. No further deterioration; resolving this flag.

flags.headline: STLD resolved amber->green -- second straight day of recovery
flags.detail: Steel Dynamics rose 2.32% to $238.68, a second consecutive recovery session following the 07-21 aluminum-segment-impairment-driven decline. Resolving this flag.

flags.headline: FAST resolved amber->green -- flat, fully digested
flags.detail: Fastenal ticked up 0.72% to $45.32, essentially flat. The 07-14 print appears fully digested with no lingering reaction; resolving this flag.
